**PC-1. Three parts, and the control-manifest lines that separate them.** (a) The **Input Adapter** reads devices, quantises, and submits `PLAYER`-origin commands as peer 1 acting on the entity the binding table binds to PlayerId 1 (CR-7). It writes no block, ever; it owns only local state (raw aim, last-acknowledged intents, hold timers, run latch, active device, context, pre-play tokens). It samples input **in the physics callback immediately before `Kernel.step()`**, so an intent submitted in frame N is frozen into tick T's P1 batch, applied in P2 and integrated by Body in P3 of the same tick — one tick of latency, never two. It never requests a Sanity, Attention or `PERCEPTION_OUT` read view: input mapping, dead-zones and aim source are HR-6 anchors and must be structurally unable to lie. (b) The **Controller Sim** registers `controller.state` (`SIM`, `persist = true`, `persist_scope = WORLD`, `scope = PER_PLAYER` keyed by PlayerId, `repl_hint = SHARED_SUMMARY`), command types `set_move_intent` and `set_aim`, the `PLAYER`-origin command **`give_up {actor}`** (`coalesce = NONE`, `max_age_ticks = 120`; validate: `loco_state == DOWNED` and no other bound seat that could revive (solo, MVP), else rejected `NOT_DOWNED`; apply: `death_tick := min(death_tick, T)`, so the existing D.14 check order does the rest in the same tick's `controller.step`: cap first, then death; PC-9) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: D7, the solo "give up and reload" action)*, and hook `controller.step` (divisor 1, `after: suit.vitals`). It writes its block in its own `apply` handlers, inside its hooks, and through four published **Class B mutators** that other owners' `apply` handlers and hooks call for cross-block writes (CR-9 a): `set_channel_ref(actor, owner_system, channel_id, face_octant)`, `clear_channel_ref(actor)`, `set_carry_ref(actor, item_id)`, `clear_carry_ref(actor)` (Interaction IA-36; Modular Ship Assembly calls `set_channel_ref(actor, ASSEMBLY, channel_id, face_octant)` and `clear_carry_ref(actor)`; `face_octant` is the owner's `octant_of(target anchor − foot)` computed at the `begin_*` apply and stored as `controller.state.channel_face`, so the facing lock of PC-4 rule 2 reads stored data that a MIRROR client has and never recomputes) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: `face_octant` added; the mutators are not kernel-invoked callables, they take the shared `WriteScope`, report with `scope.fault` and return a status that callers propagate, while every Controller callable the kernel invokes — `validate`, `apply`, `controller.step`, `controller.noise`, `snapshot`, `restore`, `post_restore`, `read_view` — receives `ctx` and ends in `return ctx.complete()`, kernel CR-19, delegated ruling R3)*; it may not submit `PLAYER`-origin commands (CR-3). It also registers the `SYSTEM`-origin command type **`stagger {actor}`** (`allowed_origins {SYSTEM}`, `coalesce = NONE`, `max_age_ticks = 120`, no player binding; rejected `NOT_STAGGERABLE` in `DOWNED`, `DEAD` or `IN_POD`; `Applied` in `STAGGERED` without extending the lock, so a stagger never chains into a stun-lock), which Suit & Equipment submits on a two-band pressure drop within `STAGGER_WINDOW_TICKS` (SE-35) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from suit-and-equipment)* (Horror Entities submits none, HE-6; PC-9), and a second divisor-1 hook **`controller.noise`** (`after: [body.integrate]`, D.13). Its `SIM` read view publishes `octant`, `run`, `gait_effective`, `aim_angle`, `aim_live`, `facing`, `loco_state`, `carry_ref`, `channel_ref`, the chest point and the hand point; `loco_state` is the name Attention (AT-31: the living-player and `IN_POD` tests) and Horror (HE-33, C-HE-18) read. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from interaction-system, modular-ship-assembly, suit-and-equipment, ship-body-and-interior-physics, attention-system, horror-entities)* (c) The **Avatar Presenter** reads `body.state` (integer position prev/curr, odometer), `controller.state` (facing, gait, locomotion state, chest point, hand point), `emitter.state` (beam lit, shape) and `tick_alpha`; for the *local* avatar only it also reads the Adapter's raw aim. It writes exactly: frame index, `flip_h`, integer position, overlay visibility, light position and light rotation — **never scale, rotation, skew or modulate on the body** (lint). *Rationale.* "Controller submits via `INPUT_SURFACE` only; never writes blocks" is true of the Adapter and false of the Controller Sim; one 

**PC-2. Input model: contexts, actions, intents, commands.** The game reads **named actions** (`StringName`, rebindable), never raw keys and never `device == 0` (4.7: `InputEvent.DEVICE_ID_MOUSE` / `DEVICE_ID_KEYBOARD`; identify devices by event type). **→ ADR** (InputMap vs a custom binding layer; edge detection by event vs polling).

*Contexts.* Exactly one context is active: `gameplay`, `chart_table`, `inspect_card`, `chat`. Entering any non-`gameplay` context sends `set_move_intent {NONE}` and clears the run latch; entering `chart_table` or `chat` also submits `cancel_channel` for a hold- **or** toggle-mode channel (in the co-op overlay the sim keeps running and a channel the player cannot see must not keep burning); entering `inspect_card` does **not** cancel the channel, so the Pillar 4 "second instrument" check on the pipe being welded is free (the zeroed move intent is not a move, the channel continues, `interact` is still tracked for hold mode and a release inside the card still cancels; `cancel` closes the card first and a second `cancel` cancels the channel). **Movement closes the card** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: D94, the Controller's context-matrix amendment adopted; the In-World Instruments fallback "buffer and replay the first move press" is void)*: a **fresh** movement input in `inspect_card` (a `move_*` key going down, or the left stick crossing `MOVE_DEADZONE` from below `MOVE_DEADZONE − MOVE_DEADZONE_EXIT`) returns the context to `gameplay` **and** submits `set_move_intent` for that octant in the same frame, in that order, so the first press both closes the card and moves the avatar (nothing is swallowed, nothing is buffered). A direction already held when the card opened is latched and does not count until it is released (or the stick falls below the exit band) and pressed again, so opening the card while walking does not close it on the next frame. A move that closes the card while a channel is running is an ordinary non-`NONE` move intent and aborts the channel exactly as it does in `gameplay`. Any transition of `loco_state` to `STAGGERED`, `DOWNED`, `DEAD` or `IN_POD` returns the context to `gameplay` on the same frame (the Adapter observes the published state; the card or overlay closes and the cursor is hidden again). Pause is reachable in every state including `DOWNED`: `chart_table` and `request_pause` are Adapter-level and never gated by `loco_state`. The full **context × action matrix** is in the table below. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; supersedes the earlier "cancel all channels on every non-`gameplay` entry" note for `inspect_card` only. Routed to Instruments and Interaction as a cross-GDD note.)* The OS cursor is **hidden and confined** in `gameplay` (HUD HS-52: no cursor in `gameplay`; the beam is the pointer) and **shown and released** in `chart_table` and `chat`; in `inspect_card` it stays **hidden and inert** (HUD HS-52: `set_aim` stays live there, and a visible cursor would be a second pointer over the beam; PC-16). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from hud-and-suit-layer, in-world-instruments-and-inspect-view; cursor visibility in `inspect_card` corrected 2026-10-27 — design review, HS-52 owns it)* Zoom is reachable from `gameplay` and `inspect_card`, and pause from `gameplay` (from `inspect_card` the first `chart_table` press closes the card, see the context return table) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; `chat` (VS-B) swallows text keys and is the only keyboard-only flow in the core loop (HR-14).

*Default bindings (`gameplay` context).*

| Action | KB+M | Gamepad | Kind | What the Adapter submits |

*Rule* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: guards (1) to (3) and (5) are enforced by the Adapter's MenuInput feed, CT-45; the layer states the behaviour it needs and consumes the events)*. (1) **Fresh press edge.** When the layer is opened by a console press or by a released governor raise, every activation on it requires a press edge that begins after the open frame; the open press's release, its auto-repeat and any carried-over held state are ignored (the Adapter latches them, CT-45). (2) **The closing activation is consumed.** When `interact` on Resume, `chart_table` or `cancel` at depth 1 closes the layer, the Adapter emits nothing from that control, to the layer or to gameplay, until it is physically released and pressed again; gameplay sees no `interact` edge until a fresh press. The layer **cannot** enforce this alone, because the Adapter polls and resyncs on resume. (3) **Echo ignored.** The Esc / Start toggle's key echo is suppressed by the Adapter, so a held Esc does not flicker the layer. (4) **No click-outside.** A `POINTER` DOWN or UP on the frozen world outside the panel does nothing (the world is a held frame, and a click there would read as an in-world action). (5) **Focus loss.** The Adapter's `FOCUS_OUT` aborts any hold fill and clears navigation state; on `FOCUS_IN` the layer stays open with the previous focus and the kernel state is unchanged.
*Why.* The next `interact` edge at the pod console is `pod_hop`, the irreversible act (WM:1225). PCI resends intents on resume and keeps a hold-mode channel only if the button is physically down, so the latch belongs to the Adapter and the layer's requirement is stated here. Key-echo detection and focus-out notifications are NOT SOURCEABLE in the engine reference (ADR candidate (e)).
*Source.* WM:1225; PCI:656-658.

**CT-43. The layer's UI clock.**
*Rule.* Layer 3 keeps its own presentation-time accumulators driven by the render delta, independent of the kernel state, of `present_time` (frozen under pause, PIPE:265) and of `SceneTree.paused` (ADR candidate (a)): one per hold gesture (starts at press, resets on release, abort or focus loss) and one drift step timer and table index (`acc_us`, `i` of D.5) that persist across opens *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, so filaments do not rewind on re-open *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Every delta is clamped to `UI_DT_MAX_MS` `[PLACEHOLDER]` so a hitch cannot complete a hold or jump the drift. The clock is presentation time (KRN CR-11) and never enters the simulation; no wall clock enters any rule except these presentation timers.
*Source.* KRN CR-11; PIPE:265.

**CT-44. The compact layout and stable order.**
*Status: **DEFERRED-REACHABLE*** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: at `H_default` every supported window (minimum 1280 x 720, registry `MIN_WINDOW`) gives `m >= 1` (D.1b "Minimum window"), so a player cannot reach the compact list at MVP; it is built and tested through the forced-`H` hook and becomes player-reachable with the Alpha HUD scale or a window delivered below the minimum. This rule, S4, the neutral ordinals, ASK-CT-10 and AC-CT-30 / AC-CT-112 are tagged accordingly.
*Rule.* The layout is **compact iff the chart multiplier `m` (D.1b, the fit inequalities) is below 1**, i.e. the frame plus its margins no longer fits the canvas; nominally that is a canvas narrower than 320 HUD px (`COMPACT_LAYOUT_MIN_CANVAS_W`, `[PLACEHOLDER]`, **derived** as `CHART_FRAME` width / 0.9, with the height twin 180 = 162 / 0.9; informational since the fit form replaced it as the input to `m`) or shorter than its twin; it is chosen at open and on canvas change, never mid-animation. The list holds at most `N_max_compact` rows (3 at the smallest canvases, D.1b). Then the spatial map is replaced by a **vertical node list** in the ART 7.4 menu grammar: one column of chamfered-rectangle items, Ground interiors, 1-px Graphite-lit borders, the bracket and bezel thickening for focus, each item carrying its 24x24 node glyph at left (the unknown tick drawn inside the silhouette exactly as on the map) and a **neutral positional ordinal** at right (a slot mark, below). The ring plate's Ground, border and rivets remain; rings and filaments are not drawn. The planned-sortie relation is a Tungsten dashed rule under the picked row (no new asset, no fill). The `IN TRANSIT` word keeps its fixed top-left position. **The compact label is a neutral positional ordinal and carries no identity.** It is one whole `ct.*` key per authored layout slot (`ct.compact.slot_<n>`, `n` = the record's position in the layout file, HOME included; no composed fragment such as a word plus a number, CT-28), rendered as the plain ordinal for that slot. It must not be a name, a dialect, a template word or a status word, and it never varies with `status`, `kind`, `template_id`, depth ring or map distance: **an UNSEEN row and a SEEN row render the identical key form**, and a record's key does not change when it becomes SEEN, BOARDED, `berthed` or ORPHAN. The key is bound to the layout slot and is not renumbered when an ABSORBED record leaves the list (a gap in the ordinals is a fact the list already shows, and a stable slot mark lets the player remember which row is which). The ordinal order is lint-checked like positions (no correlation with any Web Map & Transit cost; AC-CT-112). This is the single permitted exception to G6 and CT-14 ("except the CT-44 neutral ordinal in the compact layout, which is not a name"); it is **not** precedent for any further label. WM:1044 (UNSEEN "no dialect, no tick, no label beyond what selection shows") is read as forbidding identity, which a slot mark does not carry (text-label rule of CT-30; **accepted by Web Map & Transit**: its UNSEEN drawing row names the neutral ordinal as the single exception, ASK-CT-10 answered). **Order is a ranking proxy and is therefore fixed:** the list is in stable authored order, HOME first, derelicts in layout-file order; it is never sorted by status, distance, fuel, danger, recency or seen/unseen; an ABSORBED record leaves the list (it is part of HOME now), an ORPHAN stays in its slot, non-selectable; the relative order of the remaining rows never changes. Rows are never truncated; if the list cannot fit, the canvas minimum was mis-set.
*Source.* ART 7.4; WM:1044, :1050; CT-12, CT-16.

**Snap-to-node (the chart's own navigation, D.3).** On the spatial map, a direction press from the focused node moves focus to the nearest focusable node whose bearing falls inside the pressed direction's sector (`SNAP_SECTOR_DEG` `[PLACEHOLDER]`), widening to a half-plane if the sector is empty, else staying; no wrap, no shake, no flash; every focusable node is reachable from every other; focus order is geometry only, never ranked, and default focus is HOME. Distances used for ordering are layout distances and are never displayed (WM:1049 and ASK-AD-7 untouched). Formula, variable table and worked example in D.3 (Formulas). Stick navigation is edge-triggered at the Controller's deadzone with auto-repeat (`UI_NAV_REPEAT_MS` / `UI_NAV_REPEAT_RATE_MS` `[PLACEHOLDER]`).

- **AC-CT-117** (auto, Logic, BLOCKING) [CT-45, CT-41, EC-CT-19, EC-CT-20] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; new)* GIVEN an Adapter double that records every device read and a recorded MenuInput stream, WHEN the full panel, chart, Display & Comfort and plate flows run, THEN the layer consumes only events from the stream and never an `InputEvent`; the stream carries NAV (stick, D-pad, arrows, WASD), ACCEPT (E, A, Enter, Space) and no ACCEPT from any mouse button; a diagonal stick produces one NAV direction at a time (dominant axis, tie to vertical, no alternation without a pass through `MOVE_DEADZONE_EXIT`); a held Esc with echo produces one CLOSE; a press that closed the layer produces no further event from that control, to the layer or to gameplay, until released and pressed again (the latch), including across the resume resync; a console-open press's release and repeats produce no ACCEPT.

--- 400
*Rule.* One action calls Save/Load's `save_and_quit()`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the call's blocking behaviour is stated.)* **Call contract (this layer's requirement of Save/Load, ASK-CT-7):** the layer disables every item and **presents one frame** before it makes the call, so the disabled styling is on screen before any work; the call must return promptly with `REFUSED_DOWNED` (the same fact as `SL_QUIT_NO_WRITE_DOWNED`) or `STARTED`, and report completion through a signal or the published `save_status` (`WRITTEN`, `FAILED`) rather than by blocking the frame loop for the write, because a blocked loop freezes the panel and invites an Alt-F4 mid-write. Save/Load's timeout `SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS` is Save/Load's value (5 000 ms at authoring, range 2 000-15 000 ms); this layer's requirement *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* is that the time to a visible `FAILED` be **3 000 ms or less**, because nothing visible is allowed during the wait (SL-24) and an up-to-5-s frozen-looking panel invites an Alt-F4 mid-write: the layer asks Save/Load for a **3 000 ms default** (ASK-CT-18; Resolved 2026-10-27 — delegated ruling G2, creative-director lean, horror-tone reasons), and AC-CT-137 fails a build whose default exceeds it. **Save/Load's `save_and_quit` itself calls `request_shutdown` after `WRITTEN`, or after an unchanged-state-hash skip that writes nothing (SL-6); the layer calls nothing on that path and never waits on `WRITTEN` as an exit guard.** The item is enabled iff `PauseGate.can_save_quit` (CT-4); otherwise it is disabled (the Hull Grey disabled style of CT-VA-7). While the write runs (state `SAVE_QUIT_WAIT`, this GDD's own label and not a Save/Load name) all items are disabled, `chart_table` and `cancel` are ignored, and **nothing is added to the screen**: no spinner, no ring, no bar, no percentage, no toast, no text change (SL UI-2; SL H5; SL-24). If any bound seat is `DOWNED` or `DEAD` (the `DEAD` case is unreachable in the solo MVP, SL-6), nothing is written and the result `SL_QUIT_NO_WRITE_DOWNED` opens **`UI3_PLATE`**, the UI-3 message plate: a string stating that the newest autosave will be used (Continue restores the newest verified generation), **Back** (default focus, non-destructive) and **Quit without saving** (the destructive item, under hold-to-confirm, CT-22). A held or failed write (`SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS`, Save/Load's) lands in **`SAVE_FAILED`, which is the panel itself** with the plain word `FAILED` (a word, never colour, never Alarm Red: a save is not an instrument, HR-4) in the panel's status-line position (CT-17): the four items stay in CT-3 order, and Resume, Chart, Display & Comfort and `chart_table` all work (SL:785: "the pause panel stays"). Accepting Save & Quit there opens `UI3_PLATE` with **Retry** (default focus, non-destructive; to `SAVE_QUIT_WAIT`) and **Quit without saving** (hold). Completing the UI-3 hold calls `request_shutdown` once (CR-15) with no write; further input is ignored. `save_status` is a sticky read the layer never clears. `UI3_PLATE` is a full-bleed **message plate** (CT-28) in place of the panel *(orchestrator ruling: UI-3's string is a paragraph and the panel is too narrow for the 45-75 character reading measure at 4 of 6 canvases, ui-programmer finding X1 option (a); OQ-CT-12)*. No death language anywhere (SL:993 list).

**SL-6 — Save & Quit.** From the pause panel: `request_snapshot` while `PAUSED` (`PAUSED → SAVING → PAUSED`, `T` unchanged), write a generation of kind `QUIT`, and `request_shutdown` only after the write verifies (`WRITTEN`). The call is host-local (CR-15) and is never named a command in the MVP. Quitting is **never deferred** and bypasses the **soft** gate conditions only: if a soft condition was closed at request time the generation is written immediately and tagged `RISKY` (alternatives rejected: refusing to quit traps the player; quitting without writing silently throws away up to one interval). It does **not** bypass the seat-state hard condition: **a `QUIT` requested while any bound seat is `DOWNED` or `DEAD` writes nothing.** `save_and_quit` returns `SL_QUIT_NO_WRITE_DOWNED`, `save_status` is unchanged, and shutdown proceeds after the hold-to-confirm "quit without saving" (art bible HR-14; the look is the Chart Table's); Continue then restores the newest verified generation, which is exactly what the death stub would have done within `DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS`. The invariant this buys — **no file on disk ever holds a `DOWNED` or `DEAD` seat** — is testable (Acceptance Criteria). A `QUIT` while a seat is `DEAD` is unreachable in the solo MVP (the stub fires on the `DEAD` tick); the `DEAD` clause is for multi-seat futures. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **QUIT-then-Continue exposure (resolved, user ruling X7)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. A `QUIT` has the same blind spots as an autosave (SL-5). A `QUIT` made with a critical suit is `RISKY` with `risky_cause` containing `VITALS` (the vitals input is in `quit_risky`), so Continue followed by a death inside `DEATH_LOOP_WINDOW_TICKS` steps back past it (SL-8); a `QUIT` made a tick before `DOWNED`, or with no tell at all, is covered by the fairness route (a fall within `W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE` of Continue steps back past an `AUTO` or `EVENT` generation; *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G2, confirmed by R15)* a deliberate `QUIT` generation without `VITALS` in its `risky_cause` is exempt, because the player chose that moment and a step-back would discard a deliberate save and the session before it; a residual exposure, confirmed 2026-10-28 by delegated ruling R15, OQ-52 closed). The post-`DOWNED` refractory does not bind a `QUIT`: a deliberate quit is never refused for it (the seat-state hard condition is the only one that refuses), and a `QUIT` inside the refractory is written at once, tagged `RISKY` only through the soft inputs (AC-SL-129). **QUIT inside an open Graph window.** A `QUIT` made while a Graph warning window is open is written at once and tagged `RISKY`, so Continue restores a fault with less than `W_MIN_WARNING_S` of its warning left. This is a listed exposure with a metric (M4, Edge Cases), and it is **not** clamped: forcing the quit to wait out the window runs the wrong way, trapping the player at the menu to protect a window they can see on screen. The other hard conditions also apply: the kernel-state condition, and an in-flight write (the `QUIT` waits for it), but not the post-`DOWNED` refractory, which binds interval and event saves only *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; in `FAULTED` there is no write path (SL-22). If the write fails, the quit is held, `save_status` reads `FAILED`, and the player may retry or quit without saving by hold-to-confirm. The write waits at most `SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS` (measured on the monotonic millisecond source, which is an I/O timeout only, SL-23; polled each frame, never a blocking join, SL-10); on timeout the pause panel stays and `save_status` reads `FAILED`, the job is not abandoned, and one that completes later is simply a `QUIT` generation *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. A window-close request while `RUNNING` calls `save_and_quit()` from `RUNNING` (`RUNNING → SAVING → RUNNING`, K:164) and then `request_shutdown`, under the same rules (it saves the *current* state, so it is no rollback and no oracle); an OS kill (the task manager, power loss) falls back to the newest generation. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Close mechanism.** Alt-F4 and the title-bar close are not kills: the OS delivers the same window-close request, so they take the `save_and_quit()` path. The composition root sets `auto_accept_quit = false` so the engine does not exit on the request [UNV: the close notification and this flag are confirmed by the spike]. Save/Load is one Node built by the composition root and owned by it (not an autoload; the worker never touches it); it handles the engine's close notification **without blocking**: it records a `close_pending` intent and polls the writer each frame from `process_mode = ALWAYS` (in `RUNNING`, `PAUSED`, `LOADING` and `SAVING` alike), and `quit()` is called deferred, only after the `QUIT` generation reads `WRITTEN` (or the write was deduped, or the state is a boot-flow screen or `FAULTED`, where nothin

no HUD element displays it per write, *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*); `fail_escalated` (bool) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, HUD OQ-HS-21)* — true from the `AUTOSAVE_FAIL_ESCALATE_COUNT`-th consecutive failed write until the next `WRITTEN`, because `save_status` reads `FAILED` on every failed write and the HUD counts nothing (HS-46); Web Map publishes no depth-label field) — **computed from SIM blocks at capture** (`RISKY` stays on the read for diagnostics and the Debug Overlay; no player-facing line shows it, user ruling D82 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*); and `restore_reason` ∈ {`NEW_GAME`, `LOAD_GAME`, `DEATH_STUB`, `FAULT_RECOVERY`}, valid for the first `RUNNING` frame after `LOADING`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1)* Also published, diagnostic only: `restore_epoch` (u32, SL-23); the sim reads the value only through `kernel.clock`. **`restore_reason` is a routed request, not an existing flag:** the Pipeline GDD has no such field (a search finds zero hits), so the brief's statement that the Pipeline was already amended is false; this GDD offers the flag as *provided* and requests it of the Pipeline, HUD & Suit Layer (designed, hud-and-suit-layer.md; the request stands) and Failure Contract & Re-wake (provisional — undesigned); the HUD's UI-11 line is the MVP consumer of `DEATH_STUB` (user ruling D15) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*, and no consumer may use `DEATH_STUB` to alter hallucination content (SL-24). **There is no screenshot thumbnail** (it would capture the Perception Filter's lie, Pillar 1), **no audio cue** (any sound is attributable by the web, Pillar 3, unless Audio justifies one) and **no death screen** (art bible 7.4). - **If the window is closed while a write is in progress** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the quit waits up to `SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS` (frame-polled, SL-6), then **holds**: `save_status` reads `FAILED`, `quit_held` is published and the player leaves only through the hold-to-confirm "quit without saving"; the next open reconciles by the crash table (T-6). Rationale: one outcome for a failed or slow quit, the one SL-6 and AC-SL-45c already state; an exit after a timeout would silently discard up to one interval.
44b. **AC-SL-44b (auto) — window close in every kernel state** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. GIVEN the close request in each of: `RUNNING`, `PAUSED`, `LOADING`, `SAVING` (an autosave in flight), a bound seat `DOWNED`, `FAULTED`, and a boot-flow screen, WHEN the handler runs with `auto_accept_quit = false`, THEN: `RUNNING` and `PAUSED` write a `QUIT` generation and `quit()` is called deferred only after `WRITTEN`; `LOADING` defers the intent until the kernel is `RUNNING`; `SAVING` lets the in-flight job settle and then either dedupes (equal state hash, no second write) or writes the `QUIT` generation; `DOWNED` writes nothing, `SL_QUIT_NO_WRITE_DOWNED` is returned and the close is held for the hold-to-confirm; `FAULTED` and the boot-flow screen write nothing; in every row the handler never blocks the frame, no `quit()` is called before its row's condition holds, and an Alt-F4 injected as the same close request takes the identical path. GIVEN a write that fails or times out on a close, THEN the close is held, `save_status` reads `FAILED`, `quit_held` is true, and no exit occurs. Cites: SL-6.

content.content:
Close mechanism.** Alt-F4 and the title-bar close are not kills: the OS delivers the same window-close request, so they take the `save_and_quit()` path. The composition root sets `auto_accept_quit = false` so the engine does not exit on the request [UNV: the close notification and this flag are confirmed by the spike]. Save/Load is one Node built by the composition root and owned by it (not an autoload; the worker never touches it); it handles the engine's close notification **without blocking**: it records a `close_pending` intent and polls the writer each frame from `process_mode = ALWAYS` (in `RUNNING`, `PAUSED`, `LOADING` and `SAVING` alike), and `quit()` is called deferred, only after the `QUIT` generation reads `WRITTEN` (or the write was deduped, or the state is a boot-flow screen or `FAULTED`, where nothing is written). **Per state:** `RUNNING` and `PAUSED` run `save_and_quit()`; `LOADING` defers the intent until the kernel is `RUNNING`; `SAVING` lets the in-flight job reach `WRITTEN` or `FAILED`, then dedupes against it (state hash equal, no second write) or writes the `QUIT` generation; any bound seat `DOWNED` writes nothing and holds the close for the hold-to-confirm "quit without saving" exactly as a pause-panel quit does (`SL_QUIT_NO_WRITE_DOWNED`); `FAULTED` and boot-flow screens write nothing. **A failed or timed-out write holds the close; it does not fall through to an exit:** `save_status` reads `FAILED`, the close request is not acted on, and Save/Load publishes the host-local read `quit_held` (bool) so the Chart Table can present its hold-to-confirm (a request to the Chart Table owner, OQ-48). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, ASK-CT-11, EC-CT-38)* A window-close request while `PAUSED` under the open Chart Table (SOLO) runs `save_and_quit()` from `PAUSED` (`PAUSED → SAVING → PAUSED`) under the same rules and then `request_shutdown`; the Chart Table calls nothing and is never a second save path. On a boot-flow screen (main menu, UI-8, UI-9: no SIM state exists and the kernel is neither `RUNNING` nor `PAUSED`) Quit and window close write nothing: the process ends through boot code with no kernel call, because the kernel lists `request_shutdown` only from `RUNNING`, `PAUSED` and `FAULTED` (whether a boot-state shutdown call is wanted is the kernel owner's, ASK-CT-11); from `FAULTED`, Quit keeps `request_shutdown` and writes nothing (SL-22). If the state hash equals the newest generation's (same `T`, nothing changed) the write is skipped and shutdown proceeds. *(Orchestrator ruling: R4/R24 are silent on whether the gate applies to QUIT; three specialists agreed it must not block a deliberate quit, and proposed that it bypass every condition; the stage-5 checkpoint made the seat-state hard condition absolute, because a `DOWNED` generation would have broken the Player Fantasy's promise for up to `DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS`. Accepted exposure, from the creative director: Save & Quit before a risky door, quit, relaunch and Continue is a manual save in disguise; the friction of quit-and-relaunch is the only cost (the Zomboid comparison does not carry over, because a Zomboid death is final and a death here restarts from an autosave); determinism means it buys a retry of the player's inputs and, in a deterministic physical world, a look at one visible unknown for at most the minutes since the last autosave (Discovery is aesthetic priority 1, so this is measured, not waved through: triggers M1 to M6 in Edge Cases and AC-SL

Every hold-to-confirm also carries the **committed accessibility plan** (Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20): D80, OQ-CT-8): a two-tap alternative (PCI:835) and an adjustable hold duration, delivered at Alpha by the Controller and Accessibility Settings; the MVP layer ships the hold only, but D.2 reads its threshold from the action's effective duration (never a literal) so neither option needs a rebuild of the gesture. The action fires on the first frame the held time reaches it, not on release. Default focus on a screen with a destructive action is its non-destructive item. Release, `cancel`, `chart_table`, the pointer leaving the item, or window focus loss snaps the bar to empty in the same frame and **nothing else happens**; a new gesture needs a new press edge. The fill is a monotonic fill on the layer's UI clock (CT-43), not a flash (HR-13), and it is function rather than decoration so reduced motion does not remove it. Formula D.2.

239:**CT-3. Surface architecture: panel first, stable order.**
*Rule.* `chart_table` opens the **panel**, a right-third plate over the world (ART 7.4). The panel has exactly four items in this fixed order: **Resume, Chart, Display & Comfort, Save & Quit**. The order never changes with state. An item that cannot act is shown **disabled** (the disabled style of CT-VA-7: Hull Grey label and a dashed 1-px Hull Grey border, so it clears the 3:1 glyph floor by shape plus tone; it is no longer Graphite lit, which measured 2.8:1), never hidden *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Default focus on open is Resume (non-destructive). Chart (and any message plate) replaces the panel in a cut (a replacement is not an appearance, so it takes no fade), except under reduce flashing, where it uses the long end of the ART 7.3 fade band (`CHART_FADE_MS`, CT-13). A replacement that raises layer-3 coverage is a governed raise (the re-open governor below) *(Amended 2
*Why.* One entry point; the world stays visible under the panel as ART 7.4 specifies; the HUD (layer 2) stays visible and frozen behind the pause panel, except that an active warning mark is held ON solid (HUD HS-23; the HUD's rule, acknowledged here; the full-bleed chart covers layer 2 entirely); a stable order is a muscle-memory affordance and menu layers are anchors that must not shift (HR-6). The accepted cost is that the chart is two actions from a pause; CT-10 (a no-pick console press opens the chart) offsets it. A second `chart` action stays an Alpha playtest fallback owned by the Player Controller and is not designed here.
*Ruled (HR-13, ASK-CT-8, OQ-CT-15, OQ-CT-27): the re-open governor. A player-initiated toggle of a large plate counts toward the 3 Hz ceiling, and the layer and the kernel are rate-limited together, never the picture alone* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; creative-director ruling)*.
- **Coverage levels.** `c = 0` CLOSED; `c = 1` the panel family (`PANEL`, `SAVE_FAILED`, `DISPLAY_COMFORT` opened from the panel); `c = 2` any full-bleed in-session plate (`CHART`, `CHART_VIEW_ONLY`, `UI3_PLATE`). A **raise** is a transition that increases `c` (TX-13, TX-14, TX-16, TX-17, TX-18, TX-24, TX-25); a **lower** decreases it (TX-15, TX-19, TX-35). Boot-flow screens are not governed (no world is visible under them and they appear once per process).
- **Close and resume are never delayed.** Every lower takes effect on the press frame. In SOLO a close calls `request_resume` on that frame.

data.notes: Ten requests cover the five blockers: B1 (AC-CT-14 auto half, INTERNAL) is one Chart Table request that also aligns CT-6, EC-CT-14 and AC-CT-135 (c). B2 (CT-1, AC-CT-8) is a CONFLICT fixed in the Chart Table only, because the Controller's PC-2 context return table and AC-PCI-170 already say the first Esc in inspect_card just closes the card. B3: the glossary list is made equal to AC-WM-60's seven fields; the review log's BACK-leg item shows the creative-director wants the BACK route drawn (G2), so the layer now reads leg_origin_id, and the Web Map drawing row conforms with a one-line request. B4 has four requests: the Controller adds PC-2a (the MenuInput stream, accept = E/A/Enter/Space with no mouse accept, a latch across the resume resync, new AC-PCI-225 to 228). It also adds a per-verb ceiling cap_v, so the Chart Table's quit and Retire holds cap at 1.5 s (AC-PCI-229). I did not shrink the user-ruled 0.6-1.9 s Settings range. Margins were recomputed from the formula (0.6, 0.8, 0.95, 0.7, 0.4 s; minimum 0.4 at base 1.5 to 1.9; frames 90 and 114 at 60 fps, 46 and 58 at 30 fps). The Chart Table then closes ASK-CT-15, ASK-CT-19 and C23 and updates D.2, C-10 and AC-CT-36/127. B5: Save/Load defaults SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS to 3,000 ms (range unchanged), adds the reads quit_write_active and cancel_held_close(), and adds AC-SL-44c and 45d. The Chart Table drops its watchdog reading, makes quit_held and quit_write_active the triggers of TX-23 and TX-39, rewrites AC-CT-137 and adds AC-CT-139. The R13/R14 epoch rulings are not touched by any of these blockers, and the Chart Table quotes no epoch storage, so no epoch requests were emitted. Registry changes for the merge (the registry is not a target here): register SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS and CT_HOLD_CAP_S, add quit_write_active and cancel_held_close, and add player-controller-input.md to DELETE_MARGIN_MIN_S referenced_by. The Controller's new ACs start at 225 and its new open question is row 32; the Chart Table's new AC is 139 and its new open question is 42; Save/Load adds AC-SL-44c and 45d. Because the Chart Table GDD takes four of the ten requests, its writer should apply them in the order B1, B2, B3, B4 (input), B4 (hold cap), B5 and grep the old wording after each (G3).
